##what this file is
A portfolio, written more like a field notebook.

Less about a job title.
More about the questions underneath it.

I work on things
that have to survive
the real world.

I'm Herambh, a mechanical engineer from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. I work on chassis structures at Ather Energy, after building electric motorcycles at Ultraviolette.

My interests sit where physics meets computation: vehicle dynamics, structural design and machine learning that respects the equations. Sometimes that means a motorcycle. Sometimes a lap-time model. Sometimes a basketball court.

Out of the model.
Into the world.

## A WORKING PHILOSOPHY
THE QUESTIONS BEHIND THE WORK

01 /

Start with
the physics.

A model is only useful if it knows what it is modelling. Loads, stiffness, heat and tire behaviour are the starting point, not details to add later.In practice / chassis design + physics-informed ML

02 /

The whole system
is the problem.

A lighter frame still has to be made. A faster car still has to turn. I like the work between disciplines, where one decision changes everything downstream.In practice / vehicle-level parametric modelling

03 /

Give the idea
something to do.

Put it in a simulation. Give it a track. Ask it to follow a trajectory. Turning a question into something testable is where the interesting work starts.In practice / lap time simulation + vehicle control

04 /

Keep a little
room for play.

Some questions come from engineering. Others come from watching basketball. I'm interested in what happens when a tool from one field finds a useful problem in another.In practice / basketball spacing + density functional theory

The working evidence.

## SELECTED PROJECTS
OPEN THE ACTUAL WORK ↗

01

Lap Time Simulator

Python / FastF1 / vehicle dynamics

A 1-D point-mass model with forward-backward optimization. Track geometry and telemetry become a way to explore braking, cornering and vehicle parameters.

↗02

Battery temperature,
informed by physics.

Research / PINNs / IEEE 2023

Estimating battery temperature in dynamic driving conditions using physics-informed neural networks. Published at IEEE GlobConET.

↗03

Steering, from tire data.

MATLAB / Formula Student

Finding the operating Ackermann percentage for a Formula Student steering system using Tire Testing Consortium data.

↗04

A car that follows
the line.

Python / PID / CARLA

Longitudinal and lateral controllers for trajectory tracking and speed control, with 100% waypoint coverage in simulation.

↗05

Rethinking the vehicle's
electronic architecture.

Inter-IIT / JLR Chiplet Challenge

A chiplet-based centralized E/E architecture for connected vehicles, designed around modular scaling and neuromorphic compute.

↗
OUTPUT 01 / THE LAP TIME SIMULATOR

The model, made visible.

Saved outputs from my Python notebook: track speed, sector analysis and the simulated lap against telemetry. Australian GP 2025.

Original notebook outputs, not stock racing graphics. Tap a plot to enlarge. Open the notebook ↗

OUTPUT 02 / THE CHIPLET ARCHITECTURE

150+ ECUs, drawn as three clusters.

Diagrams from our Inter-IIT x JLR Chiplet Challenge report: a chiplet-based E/E architecture that consolidates the vehicle's distributed control units into software-defined clusters around shared memory.

Original diagrams from the team's final report. Tap a diagram to enlarge. Open the report ↗
